 This Writ Petition Coming On For Orders This

 Order
Heard learned advocate Mr. N.P.Amruthesh and learned advocate Ms. Deeksha Amruthesh for learned advocate Mr.Viswanath Sabarad for the petitioner, learned Additional Government Advocate Smt. Niloufer Akbar for respondent Nos.1 and 6 to 8, learned advocate Mr. Syed Sharukh for learned advocate Mr. S.H.Prashanth for respondent Nos.2 to 4 and learned advocate Mr. Dore Raj for respondent No.5. 
NC: 2024:KHC:18583-DB 2. The present petition is brought before the Court styling it as public interest litigation. The petitioner, who is a practising advocate, claims to have filed this petition in public spirit. 2.1 What is prayed in the petition is to direct respondent Nos.3, 4, 6, 7 and 8-authorities to consider the representations dated 16.09.2023, 05.10.2023 and 22.02.2024. Further prayer is made to direct the respondents to take action against the manufacturers of Falooda, Ice Cream, Badam Milk and other items in the property in question and further to stop such illegal and contaminated manufacturing unit. The respondents should be directed, prayed the petitioner further, not to issue Trade Licence and FSSAI Licence to the vendors who are undertaking such illegal manufacture of food/beverage items in the property, as sought to be pleaded by the petitioner. 
3. The case of the petitioner in nutshell put forth in the petition is that the petitioner knew from personal observation and investigation and also that the complaints were received by him from the citizens that in a particular premises described in the schedule, the manufacturing unit of Falooda,
Ice Cream and Badam Shake was being carried out in disregard to the food safety NC:
Sri Amruthesh N P vs State Of Karnataka on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95868927/
3 2024:KHC:18583-DB standards and that, it operated without licence and safety protocols. It is the case of the petitioner that such negligence posed a risk to public health and safety. With such basic premise of the pleadings, the prayers as above are made. 3.1. In response to the notice issued by the Court, learned Additional Government Advocate filed a memo on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 6 to 8. It is stated that respondent No.8 was deputed to inspect the premises in question and it was reported that respondent No.9 is neither in occupation of the said premises nor is running the manufacturing unit of Falooda, Ice Cream, Badam Shake etc., as alleged. 
3.2 It is further stated in the memo thus, "It was found that one Sri Mahendra Singh Chouhan was residing in the said premises and he was manufacturing Ice Creams, Falooda, Badam Milk etc., and was selling the same in a push cart under the name and style of "Jai Karnataka Milk Falooda"." 
3.3 The memo further mentions the facts as under:
"The Designated Officer, BBMP North Zone, Food Safety and Standard Authority was informed of the same. On inspection of 18.03.2024, the said Officer found several deficiencies and issued show-cause notices to the said Mahendra Singh Chouhan on NC: 2024:KHC:18583-DB 26.02.2024 and 18.03.2024. He failed to comply with the demands made in the said notices. However, he gave a reply on 30.03.2024 to the effect that since suffered financial losses, he did not intend to continue the business and hence, requested to cancellation his food registration certificate which was accordingly done and the business has been closed." 
3.4 It is stated that the closure of the premises has been confirmed by spot inspection which was carried out by the Food Safety Officer, Malleshwaram Circle. Notices issued to the person concerned, cancellation of the licence and the photographs of closure of the business are also produced along with the memo. 
4. The above stand and the factual details could not be disputed by learned advocate for the public interest petitioner except trying to harp in vain that when the petition was filed, the manufacturing business was continued. 
5. When the Court compared the date of filing of the petition and the dates and events in the investigation by the authorities, the case of the petitioner that illegal activities of manufacturing were being undertaken when the petition was filed, hardly inspires any confidence. 
NC: 2024:KHC:18583-DB 6. It clearly appeared that the public interest petition was filed without verifying the correct facts. It amounted to giving misleading facts before the Court and getting the notice issued by submitting such inaccurate and indeed, wrong facts. It is unfortunate that the public interest petition is casually filed without verifying the facts. 
7. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
